subject: biology
title: Genetic crosses and Punnett squares
key_idea: A **Punnett square** shows the possible offspring of a cross. Write the parents' alleles, then their gametes, then fill in the offspring genotypes. Read off the phenotypes, and give the result as a ratio, a probability or a percentage.

blocks.text: A genetic cross predicts the offspring of two parents for one gene. This section covers the method, using cystic fibrosis.

items.text: Two parents without cystic fibrosis have a child with it. Each must carry the recessive allele, so both are Tt (T is dominant, t is recessive).
Each gamete has only one allele. Each parent makes gametes T and t.
Put one parent's gametes across the top and the other's down the side. Each box is the genotype of one possible child.
TT and Tt do not have the disorder. tt has cystic fibrosis.
One box in four is tt: probability 1 in 4, 25% or 0.25.

items: Offspring genotypes: 1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt.
The two **carriers** (Tt) are heterozygous and do not have the disorder.
Phenotypes: 3 without the disorder to 1 with it, a ratio of 3 : 1.
Gametes have one allele each. The parents' genotypes are not written in the boxes.
Two unaffected parents with an affected child must both be heterozygous.
Heterozygous parents give a 25% chance of a recessive child.

blocks.text: Try different parents and watch the offspring. Then learn the common crosses and how to give the answer.

diagram.alt: Choose the genotypes of two pea plants to see a Punnett square of their possible offspring, tall or short.

items: A **probability** can be a fraction, a decimal or a percentage: 1 in 4, 0.25 or 25%.
A **ratio** compares the numbers: 3 : 1.
Each child is a separate chance. A 25% chance does not mean exactly one child in four.

blocks.label: Expected number of offspring
where: probability of the characteristic, as a fraction or decimal
blocks.formula: expected number = total number of offspring × probability

items.text: Three quarters are dominant, so the probability is 3 ÷ 4 = 0.75.

items.lead: Real results come out close to the ratio.
items.text: A cross gave 133 purple and 46 white plants.
133 ÷ 46 = 2.89. To the nearest whole number the ratio is 3 : 1.

items: Learn the four common crosses and their results.
Probability is a fraction, decimal or percentage. A ratio is not a probability.
Expected number = total × probability.

blocks.text: Sometimes the offspring are known and you must work out the parents. A family tree shows a characteristic over several generations.

items: Two parents without a disorder have a child with it. The allele is **recessive** and both parents are heterozygous carriers.
A person with the recessive phenotype must be homozygous recessive, such as hh.
If a very large number of offspring of an Hh parent all show the dominant phenotype, the other parent is HH.
A parent with genotype hh can only pass on h. The other parent decides whether the child can be hh.
If one parent is FF, every child inherits an F, so no child can have a recessive disorder. The probability is 0.
To have cystic fibrosis, a person must inherit two CF alleles.
If one allele in every 50 is the CF allele, the chance of inheriting one is 1/50.
The chance of two is 1/50 × 1/50 = 1/2500, so about one person in 2500 has the disorder.
Unaffected parents with an affected child are both carriers.
A homozygous dominant parent means a probability of 0 for the recessive disorder.
Multiply probabilities to find the chance of two events together.

checks.q: Two heterozygous parents (Bb) have a child. What is the probability that the child is bb?
A pea plant Rr is crossed with a plant rr. R is dominant and gives round seeds. What percentage of the offspring will have round seeds?
Two parents without cystic fibrosis have a child with it. What are the genotypes of the parents?
checks.a: Both are heterozygous (for example Tt): each carries one recessive allele.

worked_example.question:
Cystic fibrosis (CF) is an inherited disorder.

A man and a woman do not have CF.

The man and the woman have a child who has CF.

Draw a Punnett square diagram to find the probability that their next child will have CF.

Use the symbols:
T = dominant allele
t = recessive allele

Draw a ring around the genotype of any children with CF.

Probability = ___
answer_points: Both parents are shown as heterozygous (Tt).
The gametes are T, t for the woman and T, t for the man, and the offspring are TT, Tt, Tt, tt (1 unaffected, 2 carriers, 1 affected).
tt is identified (ringed) as the child with CF.
worked_example.tip: One mark for each point. A correct derivation from incorrect gametes can still score.

worked_example.question:
The allele for purple flowers is dominant to the allele for white flowers.

The scientist crossed two purple flowering pea plants.

The offspring were:
- 133 plants with purple flowers
- 46 plants with white flowers

Explain why it was possible for this cross to produce some offspring with white flowers.
answer_points: Both parents are heterozygous (Pp): each has an allele for white flowers.
So some offspring have two recessive alleles (pp) and are homozygous recessive.
worked_example.tip: One mark for the parents' genotypes and one for the offspring that inherit two recessive alleles.

worked_example.question:
Retinitis pigmentosa is a genetic condition that affects the eyes.

It is caused by a mutation to a gene. This mutation produces a recessive allele.

The condition causes rod cells in the retina to break down.

Two people who are heterozygous for retinitis pigmentosa are expecting a baby.

Draw a genetic diagram to calculate the probability that the baby will have the condition.

Use R for the normal allele and r for the allele for retinitis pigmentosa.
answer_points: The correct gametes: R, r and R, r.
The correct genotypes of the offspring: RR, Rr, Rr, rr.
worked_example.tip: Any form of diagram is allowed, not only a Punnett square. Marks for the offspring follow from your gametes.

worked_example.question:
Cystic fibrosis is an inherited condition in humans caused by a recessive allele of a gene.

There are two alleles for this gene:
• the allele for no cystic fibrosis is represented by the letter F
• the allele for cystic fibrosis is represented by the letter f.

Two heterozygous parents wanted to have a child.

Complete the genetic diagram to predict the probability of these parents having a child with cystic fibrosis.

parental phenotypes: no cystic fibrosis × no cystic fibrosis
parental genotypes: ______ × ______
gametes: ______ , ______ × ______ , ______
offspring genotypes: ______ ______ ______ ______
offspring phenotypes: ______ ______ ______ ______
probability of having a child with cystic fibrosis: ______
answer_points: Gametes: F, f and F, f.
Offspring genotypes: FF, Ff, Ff, ff.
Offspring phenotypes: no cystic fibrosis, no cystic fibrosis, no cystic fibrosis, cystic fibrosis.
Probability of a child with cystic fibrosis: 0.25 (25% or 1 in 4).
worked_example.tip: One mark for each row. The phenotypes must be in the same order as the genotypes.

blocks.text: (Supplement) A test cross finds out an unknown genotype. An organism with the dominant phenotype can be homozygous dominant or heterozygous.

items.lead: Cross it with a homozygous recessive.
items.text: Cross the unknown organism with an organism that has two recessive alleles.
If all the offspring show the dominant phenotype, the unknown organism is homozygous dominant.
If about half the offspring show the recessive phenotype, the unknown organism is heterozygous.

blocks.text: A pedigree diagram is a family tree. It shows who has a characteristic and how it passes down the generations.

items: Squares are males and circles are females. Shaded shapes have the characteristic.
Two parents without it who have a child with it: the allele is **recessive**, and both parents are heterozygous.
Two parents with it who have a child without it: the allele is **dominant**, and both parents are heterozygous.
Give the genotype of each person from their phenotype, then check it against their parents and children.

worked_example.question:
Cleft chin is a phenotype believed to be controlled by a single gene that has two alleles.
The dominant allele, N, codes for cleft chin and the recessive, n, allele codes for the absence of the cleft chin.
A woman with a cleft chin has a child with a man who also has a cleft chin.
The child does not have a cleft chin.

Use a genetic diagram to show the genotypes of the parents, the gametes they can produce and all the possible genotypes and phenotypes of their children.
answer_points: The gametes from each parent are N or n.
The offspring genotypes are NN, Nn, Nn and nn.
The offspring phenotypes are 3 with a cleft chin to 1 without a cleft chin.
worked_example.tip: A correct Punnett square scores full marks.
